sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for family tests
sections.what: Loads the testing tools, the family service, the access and relationship lists, and the stand-ins used by the tests.

sections.name: FamilyService (Family Caregiving & RBAC Matrix) (part 1)
sections.title: Fake database and service setup
sections.what: Before each test, builds fake database tables, an audit writer and a notification sender, then creates the family service with them. The fake data uses sample people such as a parent and a caregiver.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fresh setup for each test keeps tests independent.
sections.watch_out: A fake reply that a test does not set returns nothing, so a missing setup can cause confusing failures.

sections.name: FamilyService (Family Caregiving & RBAC Matrix) (part 2)
sections.title: Adding a member and share setup
sections.what: Tests that adding a member creates the profile and a matching login-free user record, and writes an audit entry. Then sets up a caregiver lookup and a fake profile for the sharing test.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shadow user must exist so that records can link to the family member.

sections.name: FamilyService (Family Caregiving & RBAC Matrix) (part 3)
sections.title: Share and revoke assertions
sections.what: Checks that sharing full access returns full access and sends two notices, one to the owner and one to the caregiver. Checks that revoking removes the permission and sends notices to both people.
sections.why: Likely reason: both people should know when access changes.
sections.watch_out: The test title says it checks permission hierarchy, but it only checks that full access is granted.

summary: Automated tests for the family service, checking that adding a member, sharing access and revoking access write the right records and send the right notices.
purpose: Protects the family access rules from accidental breakage during changes.
why: Likely reason: access rules guard health records, so the tests cover the main success paths.
how: 1) Build fake database, audit and notification objects. 2) Create the service with those fakes. 3) Run three scenarios: adding a member, sharing full access and checking the notices, and revoking access and checking the notices. 4) Check that the fake database received the expected calls.
inputs: Fake database replies for a family member, a user and a permission, plus the arguments the service passes to them.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner.
risks: The tests only cover successful paths. Refused cases, such as a non-owner trying to share a profile, are not tested here. The test named for permission hierarchy does not check the access levels.
debug: If a test fails, compare the expected call with the actual call in the output. If a notice test fails, check the wording first, since the tests match exact phrases.
